thread:
maya: Quick heads-up — AWQ quant bake for model-x-13B shows a reproducible hit on MMLU (~3.2% absolute) vs fp16. FP8 & GPTQ were fine. Logged per-layer stats and saw a weird high max-abs in a few mid layers.
ajay: 3.2% is large. Which layers are spiking? can you dump the per-channel max/mean?
maya: Pasted the short dump, top offenders were layer 22 and 24 (0-indexed). max_abs >> median by ~120x. Also see a tiny fraction of channels with extremely large values in the activation tensor.
sam_g: That screams "surgical channel outliers" — we've seen this cause AWQ/GPTQ calibration to go bad because the per-channel scale gets pulled. Did you try channel-clipping or exclude-channels?
maya: Not yet. I ran a quick probe script to scan per-head vs per-channel variance. Script: ```python
# quick scan
for l in range(L):
    a = activations[l]
    print(l, a.abs().max(), a.abs().median(), (a.abs().max()/a.abs().median()))
```
jonah: Nice. Two quick checks: 1) are these outliers present in fp16 activations (pre-quant)? 2) do they only appear for certain prompts (dataset skew)?
maya: Confirmed: fp16 shows the same spikes — so not quantization artifact. Also the spikes concentrate on a handful of tokens (rare token IDs) during long context prompts.
ajay: Probable root cause: rare-token embeddings / positional interactions causing activation bursts in attention matmul. For AWQ's per-channel scale, that will blow up quant error.
sam_g: Mitigations to try (short list): 1) channel-wise truncated clipping (percentile 99.5) before scale compute 2) surgical skiplist: force those channels to stay in fp16 or use 8-bit fallback 3) per-layer re-scaling (multiply weights by small factor to reduce dynamic range)
maya: I tried a naive clamp at 99.9 percentile, helped but still ~1.1% delta. Surgical skiplist where we revert only channels with max/median>50x got us to ~0.3% delta on MMLU.
jonah: That's promising. What's the cost in latency/size?
maya: For model-x-13B AWQ, skipping ~0.6% of channels (mostly in layers 22/24) adds ~0.4% decode cost and +0.8% model size because of mixed-format blobs. OK for Dedicated but noticeable for hosted.
ajay: Could we instead try per-channel rescale: detect offending channels, divide both weight and out-quant scale by factor f (keeping overall param distribution similar)? That keeps everything in quantized path.
sam_g: Yes but must be careful: changing weight magnitude affects optimizer/LM head fidelity for that layer. We should run a tiny calibration sweep: f in [2,4,8], measure per-layer KL to fp16 logits.
maya: Filed a tiny experiment: ran f=4 on the 4 worst channels in layer 22 -> KL dropped 70% and MMLU gap ~0.25%. I'll attach the short log below.
infra-bot: deploy-check: ran eval cluster job job-87312, 8 nodes, 1h cap — results attached.
jonah: Nice. Next steps: 1) formalize a scanner to produce candidate channel lists (threshold = max/median>X and single-token spike ratio>Y) 2) add surgical-skiplist support in AWQ loader 3) try per-channel rescale as lower-cost fallback 4) include unit eval (MMLU + common prompts) in quant bake CI.
maya: I'll open a tiny RFC/PR with the scanner + example skiplist and the f=4 rescale patch. Will also add a small flag to the loader to transparently fall back those channels to fp16.
ajay: Don't forget metrics: token-level KL, perplexity on heldout, and top-1/top-5 logits mismatch. Add rollout plan for Dedicated vs Hosted.
sam_g: And schedule a short tabletop with infra to validate storage impact — mixed-format blobs complicate caching.
maya: Cool. I'll post PR link and a follow-up thread with the chosen thresholds and instrumented metrics. Thanks all :thumbsup:
